findings.title: Launcher does not establish a working directory before exec
findings.message: Double-clicking a .command file in Finder runs it with the user's home directory as the working directory, and running it from a terminal inherits that shell's cwd. The launcher never pins a working directory, so if daily-documents.py resolves any paths relative to the current directory (rather than to its own __file__), its output will land in unpredictable locations such as $HOME.
findings.suggestion: Run the Python script from a predictable working directory, e.g. cd "$script_dir" before the exec line (or ensure daily-documents.py resolves all paths relative to its own __file__ so cwd does not matter).

findings.title: Launcher silently drops command-line arguments
findings.message: The exec line invokes daily-documents.py without forwarding "$@". The .command file is also a normal executable script, so when run from a terminal any flags or arguments the user passes (e.g. --help or a date override) are silently discarded instead of reaching daily-documents.py.
findings.suggestion: Forward arguments to the Python script: exec python3 -B "$script_dir/daily-documents.py" "$@". This is a no-op when double-clicked (no arguments) and correct when run from a shell.
